structure_and_depth.basis: Items 1-5 supply mechanisms for interpreting specialization, including how data, rewards, environments and infrastructure redistribute research work; items 6-7 then connect those mechanisms to dated people/team records and typed network edges; item 8 turns those records into four concrete organization goals. This supports a capability mapping rather than an unqualified author/company ranking. The planned person-period table, expertise-output matrix, team chronology and typed/time-stamped edge table cover the requested products and are mutually usable: paper affiliation, professional confirmation and direct versus team contribution remain separate. The two-part graph for large papers avoids an unsupported all-to-all management network. Regional samples and explicit disclosure gaps form a selection boundary without requiring an exhaustive global roster. The relevant PTT21 original professional page was inspected in its About Me, dated News and publication portions: it supplies a current public role and dated team outputs, but those facts alone do not establish an exact joining date or individual ownership of every method. Items 6 and 9 explicitly retain that distinction and item-level uncertainty. I read the complete task and outline, checked the single recorded outline-stage history and its retained draft, and verified it matches the assigned artifact. The outline states that full source reading and employment verification remain unfinished; I do not treat its source count as completed research. No required structural correction is demonstrated at this stage. The final manuscript must actually link the technical chapters to the named, dated team/person evidence; this outline pass is not factual acceptance of a completed talent map.
